one_sentence_story: Divers recalled far more words when tested in the same dry or wet spot where they learned them.
so_what_for_you: Your brain staples facts to the room around you. When a name or errand slips away, close your eyes for twenty seconds and picture the exact spot where you first thought of it.

jargon_map.plain: You recall things best in the same place where you learned them.
jargon_map.analogy: Like finding your keys faster when you stand where you walked in.

jargon_map.plain: Pulling a word from a blank page versus spotting it on a list.
jargon_map.analogy: Naming an actor cold versus picking their face from four photos.

jargon_map.plain: Closing your eyes to picture the sights and sounds of an old room.
jargon_map.analogy: Replaying a quick mental photo of your desk to jog a lost thought.

jargon_map.plain: Your memory hub stamps room sights onto every new fact you learn.
jargon_map.analogy: Like stapling a hotel postcard onto a note in a file box.
